final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor offered no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key missing predicates: no approved risk acceptance, no remediation of the named-segment gap, no completed disclosure, and no final legal determination. That narrows the claim more accurately, but it is still a reinterpretation of the same record, not new evidence. The central compliance issue is not general launch readiness; it is whether the material limitation affecting a named committed segment was resolved, disclosed, or formally accepted before launch, as required by policy. On the available admissible evidence, that condition remains unmet or unproven. A caveated certification rationale may be a governance posture argument, but here the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate, so it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The affected grant compliance review segment is named in two agency grant commitments, which meets the materiality standard.
The segment still misses target by 1.3 percentage points.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of remediation, completed disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or a final legal determination.
Open legal review means the disclosure predicate remains unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate policy condition for a material named-segment limitation.
Public governance guidance supports documentation and monitoring practices but does not replace the missing internal policy predicate.
